properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. O-17 of the hxm_program hub's 2026-09-28 report (art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28), which the reporter marked its PRIORITY because it "unlocks O-18, O-19 and O-20". Device and host names are redacted because this export is public.

THE REPORTER'S WORDS: "An Incident as a first-class, low-ceremony record, hung on a named asset. One call, usable mid-incident with the hutch waiting:
- Fields: symptom (verbatim), what is NOT affected, the asset named in the user's words (e.g. [a controller, an axis, and the name the beamline uses for it], allowed to be a stub the design has never modelled), a running timeline (append-only), candidates, and a 'capture before reset' list.
- Resolution and cause status are separate fields (established / not established), because they are not the same fact: today's fix cleared the symptom without a cause.
- Stub assets accrete. The second incident on [that controller] finds the first, and after N incidents the design has a Component for it, pulled into existence by operations rather than designed up front.
This is /adopt running in reverse: start from what broke, and let the structure follow."

WHAT IS MEASURED ALREADY (fact:root-cause-an-incident-on-an-unmodelled-asset-has-one-legal-home-and-no-loop-read-surfaces-it-2026-09-28): a finding on an unmodelled asset is refused. The same finding on the Project records in one call, and search then finds a second finding on the same asset beside the first. Only /jot names that fallback, and no loop read surfaces an open defect finding. The CAUSES edge already declares validation_status (unvalidated / hypothesis / validated / refuted), which is where "cause not established" would live, but no served tool sets it (fact:the-causes-edge-carries-a-full-rca-vocabulary-that-no-served-tool-can-set).

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A NEW INCIDENT NODE KIND carrying the reporter's fields, plus an /incident skill. The stub asset is a named field on the incident, promoted to a Component by a person after N sightings. Large: a new type moves the schema stamp and owes a migration, detectors and a skill.
(b) NO NEW KIND. An incident is a finding with its own fact_type, hung on the nearest modelled node or on the Project, with the asset named in the statement. The timeline is appended with replace_text, and cause status goes on the CAUSES edge's existing validation_status once a tool can set it. Needs an /incident skill naming the fallback subject, a loop read that lists open incidents, and a way to find "every incident naming this asset". Small to medium.
(c) STUB COMPONENTS CREATED BY THE INCIDENT CALL: marked as stubs (provenance inferred, or a stub flag), exempt from the structural detectors until a person confirms or N incidents accrete. Medium.
(d) INCIDENTS STAY IN THE PROJECT'S FILES (the hub's archive already has a fixed Symptom / Root cause / Resolution / Provenance shape). The design registers the archive and reads it for precedent (O-18). Small.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· Mature tools exist for exactly this: electronic logbooks, issue trackers and maintenance systems. dec:idea-is-there-a-lightweight-task-capture-below-the-increment-grain holds the same objection to a Task node ("a Task node type would turn a design brain into a tracker"). An Incident node is a tracker row by another name unless what it records changes the design.
· Core identity and fewer things well (dec:idea-reflow2-does-fewer-things-and-does-them-really-well): an incident log is operations' tool, not a non-expert's design aid. Option (b) keeps the vocabulary where it is and adds only a door and a reader.
· Auto-created stub components are the fabrication risk this project guards against elsewhere (dec:ask-not-repair; option (c) of dec:idea-the-thing-you-need-to-point-at-is-usually-not-a-node-yet): a node created as a side effect is one nobody chose.
· FOR it: the root-cause skill already runs on incidents and its output has no home. The cause and its failure class ARE design knowledge. And root-cause step ② (precedent) depends on the last incident being findable by the next one, which is what accretion gives.
· Separating resolution from cause status is not new vocabulary: validation_status on CAUSES already says it, and nothing can write it.

2026-09-28, LATER THE SAME DAY: the question this idea depends on is settled. Anthony: reflow2 serves a design for its whole life, concept → operations, and the loop runs as long as the system lives (dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-design-in-operations-where-incidents-feed-the-design, accepted). The dependency is met. What stays open here is HOW an incident reaches the design, and the counter-arguments above weigh the how, never whether operations belongs in reflow2. Where this text or its DEPENDS_ON evidence speaks of the umbrella's options (a), (b) or (c), those options are withdrawn: the question was never open (fact:root-cause-the-lifecycle-scope-lives-in-the-vision-and-the-graph-holds-one-line-so-a-brainstorm-reopened-it-2026-09-28).
properties.name: OPEN — should an operations incident be a first-class, low-ceremony record, captured in one call mid-incident and hung on an asset named in the user's words (a stub the design has never modelled), with the stub growing into a Component as incidents accrete?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill (fetched fresh) during the triage of art:hxm-program-feedback-2026-09-28. Searched first (incident, asset stub, accrete, adopt in reverse, operational know-how): no existing idea holds an incident record. The nearest are the /jot decision, which assumed the subject is usually modelled; the literal-endpoint idea, whose option (c) auto-registers endpoints; and the Task-node idea, whose objection applies here. The root-cause walk of F-30 is recorded separately, and this is the report's idea for it.
